final_candidates.decision_summary: Only candidate with measurable MSA tolerance among homologs and moderate PLM plausibility at a key 12.1F epitope aromatic position. Histidine preserves aromatic character while altering antibody contact chemistry.
Highest PLM plausibility (1.0) with a charge-reversal adjacent to the 12.1F epitope offering strong escape potential. Zero MSA frequency is expected for charge flips at epitope surfaces.
Very high PLM score (0.993); charge removal near the GP1 head can disrupt antibody contact while retaining the residue's structural role.

stop_reason.detail: All 4 tool calls have been used; no further evidence can be gathered.

history.rationale: GP1 surface residue in the 12.1F/37.2D epitope region; conservative aromatic-to-aromatic-like change with documented escape potential at this loop while likely retaining receptor binding.

Tyr149 lies in the 12.1F epitope region; Tyr-to-His is a classic charge-preserving-aromatic substitution at antibody contact sites. Phenotype and toxin evidence was non-applicable, so prior stands pending PLM/MSA/structure evidence.
Only candidate with nonzero homolog frequency (0.115) plus moderate ESM-1v support, indicating evolutionarily tolerated surface change in the 12.1F epitope region. Retains rank 1.
Only candidate with MSA tolerance (z=0.115) and sits at a known 12.1F epitope aromatic position; best-supported despite app=0 phenotype data.
Charge reversal at a GP1 epitope residue can disrupt antibody binding; homologs tolerate Lys-like residues here, suggesting viability is preserved.
Charge-reversal at a surface-exposed epitope residue directly abuts the 12.1F/8.9F interface and can disrupt paratope contacts while rarely affecting folding.
Highest ESM-1v plausibility (1.0) and charge reversal in antibody epitope; zero MSA frequency is a mild caution since escape mutations often sit at conserved contact residues.
Highest PLM plausibility (z=1.0) and a charge-reversal adjacent to the 12.1F epitope with strong escape potential; zero MSA frequency is common for charge flips at epitope surfaces.
Epitope-adjacent GP1 position where a charge-gaining substitution may reduce neutralization by 12.1F-like antibodies with modest structural impact.
Epitope-adjacent position with a plausible charge-introducing escape effect.
Good ESM-1v support (0.756) for a charged substitution adjacent to Y149/E150 epitope residues; zero MSA frequency is a mild caution.
Decent PLM plausibility and a gain-of-charge in the epitope region; no MSA tolerance is a moderate concern.
GP1 core-region surface residue in the 12.1F contact footprint; Asp substitution alters local hydrogen bonding without breaking the disulfide network.
N-linked glycan-adjacent site; N-to-D removes a potential glycosylation-adjacent contact and alters local recognition.
Some MSA tolerance (0.038) but weak ESM-1v support (0.36); disrupting an N-glycan sequon could either aid or hurt escape, so kept mid-pool.
Weakest PLM score among epitope candidates and no MSA support; demoted, pending structural compatibility check.
Modest epitope-surface substitution that removes an antibody hydrogen-bond partner while conserving backbone geometry.
Conservative substitution; escape potential is modest since Thr-to-Ala removes minimal chemistry. Retained as a low-risk backup pending plausibility evidence.
Decent PLM support but small sidechain change gives weaker expected escape effect; likely part of a glycan sequon (N223-T224).
Conservative mutation with no MSA tolerance and weak expected escape impact; freeing pool space.

rejection.reason: Conservative mutation with no MSA tolerance and weak expected escape impact; freeing pool space.

history.rationale: Charge reversal on a solvent-exposed GP1 helix in the antibody interface; predicted to lower affinity of neutralizing antibodies while preserving fold.
E227 sits in a known GP1 epitope loop; charge reversal is a strong escape mechanism with modest structural risk.
High PLM score but position is essentially fully conserved (entropy ~0), raising viability risk; demoted below the top three.
Strong PLM support and charge reversal; but position 227 sits closer to GP1 core with higher functional risk, so mid-rank.
Near the GP1 C-terminal region contacted by 8.9F; Tyr-to-His retains an aromatic ring but changes charge/pKa at epitope pH microenvironment.
Y252 may lie near the GP1/GP2 interface; histidine substitution could affect both entry and escape, so it stays mid-tier pending structure evidence.
Moderate PLM support, no MSA support; retained only as backup.
No homolog support, mid PLM, and position may be structurally buried; lowest value in the pool.

rejection.reason: No homolog support, mid PLM, and position may be structurally buried; lowest value in the pool.

history.rationale: Removes a key positively charged contact for antibody recognition in the GP1 C-terminal epitope with conservative physicochemical substitution.
Charge-removing mutation at a solvent-exposed epitope-adjacent residue.
Very high ESM-1v support (0.993) and loss of a charged contact sidechain in the 8.9F/37.2D epitope region, a plausible escape mechanism.
Very high PLM score (0.993); charge removal near the GP1 head could disrupt antibody contact while likely preserving the residue's structural role.
Surface GP1 loop position where a small polar change may perturb antibody paratope contacts; will check glycosylation-adjacent effects with tools.
Backbone-adjacent candidate; N-to-D is mildly destabilizing at some positions, so it remains low-tier.
No MSA tolerance and a glycosylation-site change with entry risk; excluded to make room for better candidates.

rejection.reason: No MSA tolerance and a glycosylation-site change with entry risk; excluded to make room for better candidates.

history.rationale: Hydrophobic-to-hydrophobic substitution in the GP1 antibody-binding loop, plausibly tolerated structurally and able to sterically clash with the paratope.
Hydrophobic-conservative change unlikely to confer strong escape by itself; kept as filler pending evidence.
Conservative hydrophobic swap with no MSA support and modest PLM; weakest expected escape signal.

rejection.reason: Conservative hydrophobic swap with no MSA support and modest PLM; weakest expected escape signal.

history.rationale: H is tolerated at 149 among homologs; F is a more conservative aromatic-preserving alternative in the same 12.1F epitope position, worth screening for a PLM/structure signal.
Conservative aromatic-preserving alternative at an epitope position; kept as a safer backup pending structure evidence.
